subject: Pricing ladder, SKU bundling and partner-margin reconciliation for Valence Health private offer
messages:
From: Alexa Moreno <alexa.moreno@valencehealth.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Valence Health Procurement <procurement@valencehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer pricing — ladder, SKU bundling & channel split questions

Hi Ethan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Valence is moving fast on a pilot for inference on medical imaging and procurement asked for a clear private-offer proposal we can take through our internal committee. Two asks from my side:

1) A pricing ladder (list price -> committed tiers -> incremental % off) across three commit sizes (50k, 250k, 1.2M annual). We need netbacks for our reseller to understand go-to-market economics.
2) SKU bundling options — we currently expect a mix of reserved capacity (node-hour) and burst credits; can you show a bundled SKU that would be a single line item for our invoice?

Procurement also needs a short list of evidence items they require to approve: invoice pathing for marketplace/private-offer, reseller margin breakdown, SOC2 + data handling notes, and a Po template (attached). Can you confirm what you can provide and a timeline?

Attached: Valence_PO_template.docx (procurement asked us to fill this out)

Looking to finalize by the end of next week.

Best,
Alexa

Alexa Moreno
Head of Platform Partnerships, Valence Health
-alexa.moreno@valencehealth.com-

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alexa Moreno <alexa.moreno@valencehealth.com>
Cc: Valence Health Procurement <procurement@valencehealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer pricing — ladder, SKU bundling & channel split questions

Hi Alexa — great to meet yesterday, thanks for the clear list.

High level reply now; I’ll loop in Pricing/Channel to surface exact netback math and invoice pathing.

What we can provide in the next 48 hours:
- Draft pricing ladder showing list price and three commit tiers (50k / 250k / 1.2M) with per-token/node-hour economics and expected overage bands.
- Two SKU bundling suggestions: 
  * Hybrid reserved + burst bundle (single invoice line that maps to node-hour equivalent)
  * Line-itemized bundle (reserved node-hours + burst credits) for accounting teams who want traceability.
- Channel margin workback for reseller (shows list price -> partner commission -> Redwood netback) — Ben will confirm standard reseller bands and optional uplift.
- Evidence pack: SOC2 summary, data flow diagram, DPA stub, and an example invoice pathing diagram.

I’ve attached a quick draft (redwood_pricing_ladder_draft.xlsx) to give initial numbers; it’s rough but should help procurement run initial analysis.

Next steps: if you can confirm which SKU bundling you prefer (single-line invoice vs itemized), Ben and Irene will prepare a channel-margin reconciliation and a clean XLS with the netback highlighted for each commit tier.

Thanks — talk soon.

Ethan Park
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
-e: ethan.park@redwood.inference.com | m: (415) 555-0192-

Attachment: redwood_pricing_ladder_draft.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Alexa Moreno <alexa.moreno@valencehealth.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Valence Health Procurement <procurement@valencehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer pricing — ladder, SKU bundling & channel split questions

Ethan — thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifications from procurement after an initial pass:

- Invoice pathing: we prefer a single-line invoice at the customer level (for our GL mapping) but procurement also wants a separate reconciliation file that shows how revenue flows to the reseller (MediResell) and to Redwood.
- Reseller margin: MediResell expects at least a 12% net commission at the 250k tier, scaling to 9% at 1.2M. Can you show a scenario where Redwood preserves >=75% of gross margin after commission/marketplace fees at the 1.2M tier?
- SKU bundling: prefer single-line invoice with metadata (SKU code) that maps to an internal reconciliation.

Also procurement asked for:
- A one-page list of required docs and an example invoice showing the single-line format.
- Confirmation we can do a canary rollout regionally (US-West) before global rollout.

Attached: Valence_PO_template.docx (filled with initial fields)

Can your pricing ops turn the draft into a netback table that highlights MediResell commission and marketplace fees? If you can get that by Monday EOD we can move to legal review.

Best,
Alexa
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.inference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Alexa Moreno <alexa.moreno@valencehealth.com>, Valence Health Procurement <procurement@valencehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private offer pricing — ladder, SKU bundling & channel split questions

Irene / Ben — forwarding Alexa’s procurement clarification and the draft I sent. High priority: procurement wants a single-line invoice (customer-facing) + a reconciliation that shows the reseller (MediResell) commission and Redwood netback. They also specified target commission bands (12% @250k -> 9% @1.2M).

Please do the following:
1) Irene — update the pricing ladder workbook to include a netback column that deducts: 
   - MediResell commission (use their requested bands for scenario analysis)
   - marketplace transaction fees (assume 3.5% for the marketplace path, include a second column for direct invoice where fee=0)
   - estimated cost-of-goods (node-hour run-rate) so we can show % margin retained by Redwood.

2) Ben — prepare two channel scenarios:
   A) Marketplace private-offer path (invoice through AWS/GCP marketplace) with fee and recommended reseller uplift.
   B) Direct private-offer invoice (Redwood invoices Valence, we pay MediResell commission via partner payout). For each, show netback at 50k / 250k / 1.2M.

3) Produce: 
   - A one-page sample invoice (single-line) + a separate reconciliation XLS that maps SKU->reconciliation line items.
   - A short evidence checklist for procurement (SOC2 report stub, DPA, invoice flow diagram, sample contract clause for reseller commission).

I attached a margin-workback skeleton (margin_workback_v1.xlsx) and an updated SKU bundle explanation (sku_bundles_v2.pdf). Use these as starting points. Please turn around by EOD Tuesday (18th) so we can push to legal.

Irene / Ben — keep Alexa on the thread for any clarifying q’s but mark internal calculations as internal before sharing final artifacts.

Thanks — Ethan
